logline: Two teenagers from County Sligo - one popular, one quietly brilliant - begin a secret relationship that tracks each other across years and changed circumstances as they move from school to Trinity College Dublin.

seasons.review_body: The 12-episode limited series premiered on BBC Three and Hulu in late April 2020, landing at 91 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 91 reviews, with a Metacritic score of 82. Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones stand out as an unusually well matched pair in their debut performances: Mescal earned a BAFTA for Best Actor and received an Emmy nomination, while Edgar-Jones brings Marianne's intensity, acumen, brittleness, and damage to the screen. The adaptation leans into intimacy through tight close ups, unhurried scenes, and an Eliza McLaughlin-directed attention to physical detail, often aligning more with European art cinema than prestige TV convention. The series drew strong reach, becoming the most streamed BBC programme of 2020, with 62.7 million views from April to November.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Normal People Season 1 Episode 1 premiered April 26, 2020 on BBC Three and Hulu as the opening of a 12-episode limited series that earned 91 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 91 critics and a Metacritic score of 82. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.4. Paul Mescal won BAFTA Best Actor; The Guardian praised Daisy Edgar-Jones for capturing 'all of Marianne's intensity and acumen, her brittleness and damage.' Director Lenny Abrahamson's approach is largely wordless and observational: tight close-ups, sparse dialogue, unhurried scenes that trust the leads completely. The episode establishes the secret romance between Connell and Marianne in their final year of secondary school with almost no expository scaffolding. The series became the most streamed BBC programme of 2020, with 62.7 million views from April to November.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The opening episode establishes the secret romance between Connell and Marianne in their final year of secondary school in Sligo. Director Lenny Abrahamson’s approach is largely wordless and observational, with the camera staying close and the dialogue sparse. The episode trusts its leads completely, offering almost no expository scaffolding.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Connell's drive to Marianne's house, and the first time the series makes the power dynamic between them legible without stating it.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.review_body: Normal People Season 1 Episode 12 aired May 26, 2020 on BBC Three and Hulu as the finale of a 12-episode limited series that earned 91 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 91 critics. IMDb audiences scored the series 8.4; the series became the most streamed BBC programme of 2020 with 62.7 million views. The Guardian praised Daisy Edgar-Jones for capturing 'all of Marianne's intensity and acumen, her brittleness and damage,' and Paul Mescal won BAFTA Best Actor for his performance culminating here. The finale closes the adaptation of Sally Rooney's novel at a moment that is deliberately unresolved: the relationship's status remains conditional, the future genuinely open. The ending refuses the neat romantic payoff the format might have demanded, keeping faith with the novel's refusal to comfort.
